back: A rural settlement designated by the government for planned development of services, infrastructure and jobs, to serve and stimulate the surrounding area.
Perroux (1950s): development concentrates in a centre and spreads to the region (spread effects); backwash effects are the negative drain on the region.

front: Aims of the growth point policy?
back: Spread development, create jobs, provide services near people, reduce rural-urban migration, concentrate investment efficiently.

front: Typical services at a growth point?
back: Schools, clinic, police, shops, produce market, mill, bank agency or mobile money, fuel, bus terminus, water, electricity.
Better access to services and markets for rural people; some jobs; some centres have grown into towns.
Limited jobs and industry, unreliable electricity and water, unsold stands, limited funds, weak links with farmers, continued migration.
Grain milling, oil pressing, cotton ginning, brick and furniture making, fruit drying, crafts and tourism, solar services.
Reliable infrastructure, incentives, links with farmers, skills training, more funds for local authorities, better transport.
